projects.title: GivEnergy Hybrid Gen3 LV Inverter Firmware Matching Decompilation
projects.game: GivEnergy Hybrid Gen3 LV inverter firmware (ARM A316 and DSP D316 images)
projects.platform: GivEnergy Hybrid Gen3 LV inverter: STM32F105/107 ARM A316 and TMS320F2806x DSP D316. Matching builds were verified on macOS Apple Silicon with Wine and the native macOS TI object tools; the maintainer says Linux with Wine should work but has not tried it.
projects.status: The public v1.0.0 release was published 2026-10-16. The README reports byte-identical rebuilds of both images: 99.0% of A316 image bytes and 74.1% of D316 words come from recovered source; the remaining image content is vendor libraries, a region table, and linker padding. The maintainer says the work has only been tested as a rebuild, not as firmware to flash.
projects.summary: Matching C and assembly decompilation of the ARM and DSP firmware in GivEnergy Hybrid Gen3 LV inverters. Build gates use the original Keil and TI toolchains and compare complete output images against the matching retail files. The repository contains no firmware images. Its MIT license covers the author’s tools and documentation; reproduced GivEnergy firmware and third-party code remain under their original rights.
projects.strategy: Matching C/assembly decompilation rebuilt with the original vendor compiler and linker toolchains, then compared byte-for-byte with the target images.
projects.source_available: Public C/assembly source, analysis notes, build tools, and comparison gates; no original firmware images are included. The repository MIT license covers the author’s tooling, documentation, configuration, and annotations, while reproduced GivEnergy and third-party code retain their original rights.

projects.title: Pokéwalker Firmware Matching Decompilation
projects.platform: Nintendo Pokéwalker accessory firmware on the Renesas H8/38606. The maintainer reports successful reconstruction builds on macOS Arm64 and Windows x86_64; macOS runs the 32-bit Windows Renesas tools through Wine and Rosetta.
projects.status: The maintainer describes the matching reconstruction as complete. With a supported Renesas HEW toolchain and the retail artwork, the source can be built and checked against the retail firmware hash. The README does not name a retail firmware version, and no tagged GitHub release is listed.
projects.summary: A human-readable C source reconstruction of the Pokéwalker firmware, based on reverse engineering, disassembly, and decompilation of the retail firmware and related HeartGold/SoulSilver software. The repository does not distribute retail firmware or artwork; users supply lawful local copies or use permissively licensed placeholders. CC0 applies only to the project authors’ own material.
projects.strategy: Matching decompilation of the H8 firmware into separately compiled C modules, using the supported Renesas toolchain and retail-hash verification.
projects.source_available: Public reconstruction source, build and verification tools, and documentation under CC0 for author-created material. Retail firmware, extracted artwork, and the Renesas compiler are not distributed.

projects.strategy: Reimplementation of Wii IOS system software, based on Team Twiizers’ mini replacement, with a modular subsystem design.

projects.title: Mufus (Rufus Workflow Reimplementation for macOS)
projects.platform: Native macOS 12+ application for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. The maintainer says validation was performed on Apple Silicon macOS 26.4.1 and with the Intel executable under Rosetta; created USB media targets compatible UEFI PCs.
projects.status: Early public release v1.0.1 was published 2026-10-16. The README lists automated tests on disposable disk images and says physical USB boot testing and Apple notarization remain outstanding. The README says the app was developed after analysis of a Rufus 4.15 executable and is not a complete replacement for every Rufus feature.
projects.summary: A native Swift/SwiftUI macOS utility that recreates selected Rufus workflows: writing hybrid Linux and raw images, preparing Windows 10/11 UEFI installation media, and formatting external drives. Its repository includes the investigation notes, a GPL-3.0-or-later license, and the bundled wimlib source and license notices.
projects.strategy: Independent native application built after reverse engineering the Rufus 4.15 executable and reviewing public Rufus source for Windows-specific workflow behavior.
projects.source_available: Public Swift source and v1.0.1 release under GPL-3.0-or-later. The repository also includes wimlib source and corresponding license notices.

projects.title: oxpinyin (libpinyin C ABI Reimplementation in Rust)
projects.game: libpinyin 15-series C ABI and output behavior
projects.platform: Linux distributions including Fedora Rawhide, Debian testing, and NixOS are listed as parity-tested. The README also documents macOS build paths through Homebrew; Windows support is not documented.
projects.status: Stage 1 is marked complete: the maintainer reports 1,571/1,571 corpus rows and 79 exported symbols, with one remaining gap because the differential suite does not exercise the full exported ABI. Stage 2 is in progress; no GitHub release is listed. Repository activity continued through 2026-10-16.
projects.summary: A pure-Rust reimplementation of libpinyin that provides a drop-in libpinyin.so.15 and the same C ABI. The maintainer uses a pinned, source-built libpinyin oracle and differential tests; the project is GPL-3.0-or-later.
projects.strategy: Clean-room Rust reimplementation of libpinyin APIs with C ABI compatibility and differential output comparison against a pinned libpinyin oracle.
projects.source_available: Public Rust source under GPL-3.0-or-later, with build instructions, differential tests, and project status documentation.

projects.title: Grit (Git Engine and Client Reimplementation in Rust)
projects.game: Git version-control semantics and repository formats
projects.platform: Native CLI builds for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Git-compatible on-disk repositories and wire behavior are maintained for implemented features; the README does not claim full Git command-line parity.
projects.status: Active; release v0.5.10 was published 2026-10-16. The project now focuses on a linkable Git engine and a modern CLI for common workflows. Its earlier Git-identical CLI and ported Git test harness were removed; the current CLI has a smaller command set.
projects.summary: A Rust reimplementation of core Git semantics, including repository objects, diffing, refs, revision walking, merge, configuration, and smart HTTP serving. The shipped client is workflow-oriented and keeps repository and protocol compatibility for the features it implements. The source is MIT-licensed.
projects.strategy: Reimplement Git core behavior in a linkable Rust library and a modern client, validating implemented behavior against the system Git binary and maintaining on-disk and wire compatibility.
projects.source_available: Public Rust source and v0.5.10 release under MIT.

projects.title: openfirma (AutoFirma Client Reimplementation)
projects.game: AutoFirma Spanish electronic-signature client (AutoFirma 1.9 is used for some golden comparisons)
projects.platform: The project documents a Windows, macOS, and Linux desktop target. CI runs on all three; Windows system-certificate signing is compiled but runtime-untested, and the macOS keychain backend currently lists certificates but refuses signing pending tests.
projects.status: Very early, phase 1 per the maintainer README; no GitHub release is listed. The README reports working CAdES/PAdES/XAdES baseline subsets, crosschecks with OpenSSL/qpdf/xmlsec1, and structural golden comparisons with AutoFirma. Real government-site browser integration still lacks its WSS transport; FacturaE and several XAdES shapes are not started.
projects.summary: An independent Rust reimplementation of the Spanish government’s AutoFirma electronic-signature client. It implements a CLI and GUI over a shared core for selected CAdES, PAdES, XAdES, verification, and certificate-store workflows; the project states that it does not copy AutoFirma Java code. Dual-licensed GPL-2.0-or-later or EUPL-1.1.
projects.strategy: Independent Rust implementation of AutoFirma signing, verification, keystore, and browser-dispatch behavior, with format-level crosschecks and golden comparisons against AutoFirma 1.9.
projects.source_available: Public Rust source and documentation; the maintainer declares GPL-2.0-or-later or EUPL-1.1. The project has no GitHub release yet.

projects.title: Konica Minolta bizhub 206 CUPS Filter Reimplementation
projects.platform: Linux CUPS hosts using glibc or musl, including Alpine; output targets the Konica Minolta bizhub 206 printer. The filter is a C11 program with no third-party runtime dependencies.
projects.status: No tagged GitHub release was listed. The README reports byte-exact output on 60 differential cases, tests through real pdftoraster input, glibc and Alpine/musl verification, and five physical print sheets through a temporary CUPS queue. GitHub metadata reports no detected license, and the repository README does not declare reuse terms.
projects.summary: A C reimplementation of the device-stream side of Konica Minolta’s 245igdirf CUPS filter for bizhub 206. It reconstructs raster framing, color conversion, halftoning, and JBIG1 encoding from disassembly and runtime captures; comparison against the vendor filter is byte-exact except for documented uninitialized padding bytes.
projects.strategy: Reverse engineer the proprietary CUPS filter from disassembly and runtime captures, then reproduce its raster-to-device-stream output in portable C.
projects.source_available: Public C source and detailed reverse-engineering notes; no repository-wide license was detected by GitHub and no reuse license was found in the README or root file listing.
projects.subtype: Printer CUPS filter and device protocol

projects.title: exiftool-rs (ExifTool 13.59 Reimplementation)
projects.game: ExifTool Perl v13.59 behavior and metadata formats
projects.platform: Portable Rust CLI and library with an optional egui GUI; the README documents builds for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
projects.status: Release v0.10.0 was published 2026-10-16. The README reports byte-for-byte read parity with ExifTool 13.59 on its 195-file corpus, across tag names, values, groups, and repeated-instance output. It lists 93 readers and 15 writers but says most write cases do not yet match Perl ExifTool. The README declares GPL-3.0-or-later; GitHub API license detection is NOASSERTION.
projects.summary: A Rust reimplementation of ExifTool v13.59 with library, CLI, and optional GUI. It generates tag tables from Perl ExifTool sources and ports conversions into Rust; the maintainer documents a broad read feature set and clearly limits its current writer parity.
projects.strategy: Reimplement ExifTool metadata readers, writers, and conversions in Rust, using generated tables and a parity harness against Perl ExifTool 13.59.
projects.source_available: Public Rust source and v0.10.0 release. The repository LICENSE and README specify GPL-3.0-or-later; GitHub’s repository API returned NOASSERTION for automatic license detection.

projects.title: ReticulumKit (Swift Reticulum Protocol Stack Implementation)

projects.platform: iOS 16+ and macOS 13+; Swift 6.1+ and Xcode 16+ are listed as requirements. The protocol can use TCP, UDP multicast, and an RNode LoRa radio over Bluetooth LE.
projects.status: The README describes alpha status as v0.1.0 and says the implementation has been wire-tested against Python Reticulum. The GitHub release API lists no published release; latest source push was 2026-05-24.
projects.summary: An independent pure-Swift implementation of the Reticulum cryptographic networking stack for Apple platforms. It implements identities, packet encoding, announces, encrypted links, routing, and TCP, local UDP multicast, and RNode radio interfaces. The source is MIT-licensed.
projects.strategy: Clean-room Swift protocol-stack implementation checked for wire interoperability with the reference Python RNS implementation.
projects.source_available: Public Swift package source under MIT; README marks the API as alpha and there is no published GitHub release.

projects.title: Maxima (Minima Communication Protocol Reimplementation)
projects.game: Minima Maxima communication layer (protocol revision not specified)
projects.platform: A Java 11 shared core, an always-on Android transport, and a headless Linux/PC server; the user guide also lists Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, and Linux clients. The README says on-device Android behavior remains unverified.
projects.status: The maintainer README says the protocol reimplementation is complete and verified against a live Minima network. It reports 63/63 codec parity, live send/receive, and relay interoperability; Android app behavior on a physical device remains unverified. Release v0.6.143 for the companion Parlons app was published 2026-10-16. GitHub metadata reports no declared license.
projects.summary: An original wire-compatible reimplementation of Minima’s Maxima communications layer, with a JVM core, relay/directory/mailbox server, and Android transport. The maintainer includes reference-generated vectors and reports interoperability with an unmodified Minima node. The public repository does not declare a reuse license.
projects.strategy: Implement the Minima Maxima framing, identity, cryptography, send/receive, relay, and mailbox behavior in Java, checking golden vectors and live traffic against the reference implementation.
projects.source_available: Public Java, Android, and server source plus published Parlons releases; GitHub repository metadata and root-file listing show no declared license.
projects.subtype: Blockchain communication protocol and service stack
